answer: Plant each new identity in a small juniper hedge: seven strangers grouped at random who share one locked stake, a bridge of mutual fate. At the nadir of trust a newcomer starts with nothing, and its hedge-mates — who lose their own stake if any member is proven fake — vet it live before it can earn. A farm's hundred clones are scattered across a hundred hedges, each needing its own stake and surviving six strangers' scrutiny, so every fake costs a full stake plus a fresh vetting, and one farm cannot pool its clones into a single safe hedge.
